paper_metadata.title: Development and validation of a clinical model (DREAM-LDL) for poststroke cognitive impairment at 6 months

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a multicenter approach with consecutive recruitment of patients with a clearly defined diagnosis (AIS). Inclusion/exclusion criteria and baseline characteristics are well-documented, and the sample size is adequate for the analysis performed.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: records of consecutive patients with confirmed AIS treated at 4 regional stroke centers from June 2017 to February 2018 were retrospectively reviewed.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical setting (4 regional stroke centers) and the specific patient population (AIS).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The records of consecutive patients with confirmed AIS treated at 4 regional stroke centers... were retrospectively reviewed.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is the gold standard for reducing selection bias in prognosis studies.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from June 2017 to February 2018
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment

items.evidence_snippet: 4 stroke centers in Shanghai
items.reasoning: The geographic location and type of facilities are clearly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: AIS was diagnosed by a neurologist according to the World Health Organization definition... Patients with pre-existing cognitive impairment before AIS according to their medical records and patients with severe cognitive impairment or aphasia who might be unable to undertake MoCA assessment were excluded.
items.reasoning: The study provides both positive inclusion criteria (WHO definition) and specific exclusion criteria (pre-existing dementia, aphasia).

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Demographics and baseline characteristics of the PSCI and non-PSCI patients at 6 months were described in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive list of age, sex, BMI, education, stroke severity (NIHSS), and comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study only includes patients who completed both the baseline and 6-month MoCA. While the reasons for exclusion (aphasia/severe impairment) are noted, the retrospective nature makes it difficult to determine if those lost to follow-up differed significantly from those who completed the study.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (baseline MoCA) and other predictors (LDL-C, NIHSS, Glucose) are objective clinical measurements or validated scales, measured consistently across centers.

items.reasoning: The study uses the MoCA and NIHSS, which are internationally validated and reliable instruments in stroke research.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

items.reasoning: While some cut-points (like LDL-C <1.8) are based on clinical guidelines, others (like Age >63) appear to be derived from the study's own median/distribution, which is data-dependent.
